 VALDOSTA, Ga. -- With Thanksgiving just days away, families across South Georgia are feeling added pressure to put food on the table as local organizations report growing demand for assistance and a federal proposal could put SNAP benefits at risk for millions of Americans.
 Michael Smith, CEO and president of Greater Valdosta United Way, said more working families are seeking help for the first time. “We’re seeing a lot more two-household incomes, full-time employees that are coming by needing assistance for the first time ever,” Smith said.
 A new United Way report found 47 percent of Lowndes County households struggled to afford basic necessities in 2024. With children out of school next week, some families will also lose access to school meals and face higher grocery costs.
 “Families who rely on school breakfast and school lunch can no longer count on those, and so they’re having to stretch budgets that much further,” said Eliza McCall of Second Harvest of South Georgia.
 At the same time, a U.S. Department of Agriculture proposal could change who qualifies for SNAP benefits. The agency estimates 6.3 million Americans could lose benefits.
 In a statement sent to FOX 49, a USDA spokesperson said: “It has allowed states to take short cuts, error rates to balloon, and those households with income and assets far above federal limits access to a benefit meant for the neediest among us. Correcting this loophole is long overdue.”
 Second Harvest of South Georgia raised concerns about how changes to SNAP eligibility could affect children’s meal programs. “It’s gonna cost us more to take fewer children,” McCall said.
 Local organizations are increasing food distributions ahead of Thanksgiving. Smith said even small amounts of support can make a difference for families. “You’re not talking a lot of money that can really give some people a little bit of peace and stability and hope for the holidays,” he said.
 Second Harvest of South Georgia is hosting its “Thanksgiving for Thousands” food distribution Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Valdosta High School. The event is scheduled to begin at 7:30 a.m., with food available first come, first served.
